convertibility_reason: Uses only standard MT5 trade library classes (CTrade, CSymbolInfo, CAccountInfo, CPositionInfo, CMoneyFixedMargin). No custom indicators, no external .mqh libraries for trading logic, no iCustom calls. Entry/exit logic is simple random comparison. Fixed margin-based position sizing via standard MoneyFixedMargin class. Only complexity is hedging account requirement.

derived_values.name: m_adjusted_point - point value adjusted for 3/5 digit brokers
derived_values.formula: m_symbol.Point()*digits_adjust where digits_adjust=10 if Digits==3||5 else 1

other_exits: No signal-based exit logic - positions are opened with random SL/TP and held until SL or TP is hit. No trailing stop, no partial close, no time-based exit.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: CMoneyFixedMargin calculates lot size based on InpPercentRisk (default 10%) of free margin. CheckOpenLong/CheckOpenShort returns calculated lot. If CheckVolume validates the lot, trade is placed. No explicit max_positions limit - multiple positions can stack on every tick where random values match.

custom_logic_notes: This is a pure gambling/random EA. Entry signals are generated by comparing two independent random integers (0-100 range). If value1==value2, a BUY is opened. If value3==value4, a SELL is opened. SL and TP sizes are random integers between 10 and 100 pips (using m_adjusted_point for digit normalization). The EA requires a hedging account (ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE_RETAIL_HEDGING) and fails to initialize on netting accounts. There is no position limit - on every tick, new random comparisons are made, so multiple positions can accumulate rapidly. The probability of a trade on any given tick is approximately 1/101 for each direction. MathSrand is seeded with GetTickCount() in OnInit. The GetRand function uses MathRand() in a loop until the value falls within [vFrom, vTo] range - this is inefficient and potentially slow for narrow ranges.
python_conversion_notes: No indicators to convert. Trading logic is trivially simple: compare two random numbers, open market order if equal. Key conversion points: (1) Replace CMoneyFixedMargin with equivalent margin-based lot calculation - need to replicate CheckOpenLong/CheckOpenShort logic that calculates lot from risk percent and SL distance. (2) m_adjusted_point digit adjustment must be replicated for proper pip calculation. (3) The random number generation uses MathRand seeded with GetTickCount - use Python random.randint(0,100) for value comparisons and random.randint(10,100) for SL/TP. (4) Hedging account check can be omitted or replaced with a config flag. (5) No technical analysis whatsoever - this is essentially a Monte Carlo trading simulation. (6) Watch for position stacking - no check for existing positions means unlimited positions can open per tick if random matches occur.
